fine_trace.code: hb_blob_t *blob = hb_blob_create ((const char *)data, size, HB_MEMORY_MODE_READONLY, NULL, NULL);
fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled font bytes are wrapped in a blob and used to create a face; the font is then passed to hb_subset.
A subset plan is created from the attacker-controlled face; the plan drives which tables are subset and which glyphs are retained.
The glyf table is selected for subsetting; its subset routine invokes the serializer that builds the packed object map.
A new object_t is allocated from the pool; hb_pool_t::alloc zeroes the whole struct, so links.length=0 and links.arrayZ_=nullptr.
Links are appended to the current object's links vector; hb_vector_t::push calls resize which zeroes the new element, then the four link fields are assigned.
The object pointer is looked up in packed_map; get() calls bucket_for() which calls hb_hash(key) on the object_t pointer.

object_t::hash reads links.as_bytes() which is hb_bytes_t(arrayZ(), length * item_size); the bytes of the link_t array are hashed, and any uninitialized padding or stale bytes in the realloc'd buffer are read by MSAN.

The hash of the object_t pointer is used to index into the hashmap; the uninitialized bytes read by object_t::hash propagate into the hash value and trigger the MSAN use-of-uninitialized-value report.
